name: manual_a6ff45
claim: A "clean replay" or history-rewrite operation on a branch preserves file content but changes every commit SHA -- verify preserved work by checking actual file/function content on the new branch (grep for the specific fix, or diff against known-good text), not by looking for the original commit SHA in the new history, which will never be found even when the work is fully intact. When a fresh review pass on a post-rewrite branch resurfaces findings that look identical to already-fixed ones, check current code first: it is very likely a new, deeper pass finding genuinely new issues (or tightening a prior fix), not evidence the rewrite lost anything.

decisions.notes: Concrete post-rewrite verification principle from this exact PR258->PR260 sequence.
